solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Letter from Greece written by an old music producer

indicators.note: in a down-style charade sense, one piece is set down beside the next, so the pieces follow on

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A letter from Greece penned by an elderly record producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'music producer' is not a person in the music business but an instrument that makes music.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano is an instrument, something that literally produces music when played.

clue.text: Persons working keep going

indicators.note: working means being worked over or processed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People in employment carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: To press on is a phrasal verb meaning to continue despite difficulty.

clue.text: An affair those compromised, somehow or another

indicators.note: compromised means damaged or weakened, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An affair put those people at risk, in some way or other.
explanation.definitionFit: After a fashion is an idiom meaning in some way, though not very well.

clue.text: Informed about article ahead of social event

indicators.note: in a down clue ahead of means placed above, so earlier in the answer

parts.note: on means about, as in a book on birds
the is the definite article
a ball is a formal dance, a social event

explanation.surface: Someone well briefed on an item before a party.
explanation.definitionFit: On the ball is an idiom for alert and well informed.

clue.text: Caretaker's rent reduced on New Year's Day

definitions.note: read as 'caretaker is', so the definition is the noun caretaker

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: New Year's Day is Jan 1, with the figure 1 written as the letter I

indicators.note: reduced tells us the word for rent is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: rent, as a past participle, means torn

explanation.surface: A caretaker's rent has been lowered on the first of January.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid to a landlord but is the past participle of rend, torn.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor is a synonym for a caretaker who looks after a building.

clue.text: Precisely in that way, I agree

definitions.meaning: a reply meaning quite right, I agree

explanation.definitionFit: Just so describes something arranged exactly right, and is also a phrase of agreement.

clue.text: Short sleep in between, a priority

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Fitting a quick snooze in between tasks is a priority.
explanation.definitionFit: A nap is a brief sleep, typically during the day.

clue.text: Become less active in ancestral home after shock

indicators.note: after tells us the home piece comes after the shock piece

parts.note: to take aback is to shock or surprise
a seat is a family's country residence, as in a country seat

explanation.surface: Someone becomes less active in the family home after a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a back seat is an idiom meaning to withdraw from an active or leading role.

clue.text: Uncommon poison copper overlooked

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so the copper symbol is dropped from the poison

parts.note: curare is a plant poison used on arrow tips
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A rare poison was missed by the police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare is a synonym for uncommon, seldom found.

clue.text: Large landed properties in European countries

parts.note: states are countries or nations

explanation.surface: Big country houses with land found across Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Estates are large areas of land owned by one person or family, usually with a big house.

clue.text: All right to go in for every game

indicators.note: to go in tells us the first piece is placed inside the word for every

parts.note: per means each or every, as in 'per person'
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees to play the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a card game played for stakes.

clue.text: Far superior ways associated with a school principal

parts.note: streets are roads or ways
a head, or head teacher, runs a school

explanation.surface: Roads linked to a head teacher are much better than others.
explanation.walkthrough: STREETS AHEAD is a British idiom meaning far better than the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Streets ahead is an idiom for being much better than others, well in the lead.

clue.text: Clown in RU team, second to be dismissed

indicators.note: to be dismissed means sent off, so the letter for second is removed

parts.note: Harlequins is a London rugby union club

explanation.surface: A joker in a rugby side is about to be sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is rugby union; Harlequins is a famous London club.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlequin is a stock clown character of pantomime and commedia dell'arte.

clue.text: Definitely not included in declaration of earnings

indicators.note: included in says the answer sits within the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Something is certainly not part of a tax return.
explanation.definitionFit: No fear is an informal British exclamation meaning certainly not, no way.

clue.text: Decree, one in Jordan judge disregarded

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for one goes inside the shortened name
disregarded means the letter for judge is ignored and dropped from the name

parts.note: the numeral one is written as the letter I

explanation.surface: A decree issued by one judge in Jordan was ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to order or decree something officially.

clue.text: Garden centre in northern Surrey, refurbished

indicators.note: refurbished means done up and remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden centre in the north of Surrey has been done up.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a place where plants are raised and sold, a garden centre.

clue.text: Entertained, in the morning, American editor

parts.note: a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: A US editor was entertained in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Amused means entertained or made to laugh.

clue.text: UK releases my suspect, a political refugee

indicators.note: suspect, as an adjective, means dubious or not genuine, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Britain frees my suspected criminal, who claims to be a refugee.
explanation.definitionFit: An asylum seeker is a person fleeing persecution who asks another country for protection.

clue.text: Notice caps raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the word is turned around

parts.note: tops are caps or lids

explanation.surface: A sign says caps have gone up in price.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot is a synonym for to notice or catch sight of.

clue.text: Indicate fielding position

definitions.meaning: to indicate a direction with a finger
a cricket fielding position close to the batsman on the off side

explanation.surface: A captain shows where a fielder should stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Point means to show or indicate, and is also the name of a cricket fielding position.

clue.text: Drink with group of players no end

indicators.note: no end means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: A drink with the team that goes on endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a hot drink made by infusing leaves.

clue.text: Pinch milk

definitions.meaning: to milk a cow is to ... its udders; also to ... money out of someone

explanation.definitionFit: Squeeze means to pinch or press, and to extract or exploit, as when milking someone for cash.

clue.text: Drank a rum after initially taking pot

indicators.note: after tells us the rearranged letters come after that opening letter
initially points to the opening letter of the word taking
rum is an old British adjective for strange or odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone drank rum after first picking up a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the adjective meaning odd, an anagram signal: DRANKA becomes ANKARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large drinking mug, and pot is an old word for such a beer mug.

clue.text: Smart tyrant abroad getting rid of leader of rebellion

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the remaining letters are rearranged
getting rid of tells us one letter is removed from the word tyrant
leader of points to the opening letter of rebellion

explanation.surface: A well-dressed despot overseas is quashing a rebel uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R (leader of rebellion) from TYRANT to leave TYANT, which 'abroad' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty is an informal word for neat and smart in dress.
